description: Generate ready-to-render chart code for a dataset via the BIC backend: the data shape is profiled locally, the backend picks a suitable chart type (or honors chart_type), and returns code that has passed the backend's eligibility gates and quality checks. Requires a trial or paid BIC account (license env vars / credentials file). The returned D3 code is a portable render(container, data, options) function meant to be MERGED into your own app; an integration contract describes exactly how to call it. A standalone HTML preview and file output are optional.

chart_type.description: Preferred chart type by name (honored unless the data shape disqualifies it).

csv_path.description: Path to a CSV file (header row required).

culture.description: The language the chart's own text should be written in - titles, axis labels, legends, notes - as a BCP 47 tag such as 'de-DE', 'fr' or 'ja-JP'. Default 'en-US'. Set it from the end user's locale when you know it; it does not translate the data.

data.description: A pre-typed {columns, rows} table — the shape a Fabric DAX query / dataframe already has. Alternative to csv_path/csv_text; when columns carry isMeasure/format/description the shape matches PBI fidelity with no guessing.

dataType.description: Known type (DAX/semantic-model callers have it); omit to infer from values.

description.description: Column description from the model → modelDesc.

format.description: Format string from the model (e.g. "$#,##0") → modelFormat.

isMeasure.description: Known measure/dimension role; omit to apply the numeric-non-identifier heuristic. A semantic-model caller should set this.

rows.description: Rows as positional arrays aligned to columns, OR objects keyed by column name.

descriptions.description: Per-column human DESCRIPTION — gives the model semantic context the bare column name lacks.

dimensions.description: Columns to treat as DIMENSIONS (a PBI category/axis well — fields to group/break by). Use for numeric codes/years that should NOT be aggregated.

font_family.description: CSS font family for the chart's own text — titles, axis labels, tick labels, legends (e.g. 'Segoe UI' or a stack like 'Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif'). Pass this ONLY when the user has named a font or you are matching a stated house style — do NOT infer one from the data, the project, or your own preference. Omitting it is a proven no-op: the engine picks. Applies to whichever renderer is chosen (D3, Plotly, matplotlib and Vega each get an equivalent instruction), and an unavailable family falls back to a web-safe stack rather than failing.

forbid_derived_columns.description: True = show only fields present in the data (plus required_columns) — no per-capita, share-of-total, index, rank or z-score columns the engine would otherwise add. Use when your app owns the analytics and the chart is only the display.

formats.description: Per-column number/date FORMAT STRING (e.g. {"Revenue":"$#,##0","Margin":"0.0%"}). PBI supplies these from its model; a CSV can't, so provide them to steer number formatting.

group_by.description: Columns that are the PRIMARY series/breakdown (the PBI 'Group by' well); the backend leads the visualization with these.

include_code.description: Include the full code in the response — governs BOTH the text block and structuredContent.code. Default: true, or FALSE when out_dir is given (the code is then already on disk, and a large chart's code can overflow a client's tool-output limit). Set it explicitly to override either default.

language.description: Project source language: with no concrete `renderer`, the backend auto-picks a renderer WITHIN this language (javascript/typescript → D3/Vega, python → Plotly/matplotlib). Omit to AUTO-DETECT from the working dir.

level_of_detail.description: How much of the data the user wants to SEE. ASK THEM — do not infer it from the data or from your own preference; it is a question about what they want, and they can answer it in one word. 'High' = every observation drawn as its own mark (scatter, beeswarm, strip). 'Medium' = every row used, but shown as a distribution (box, violin, histogram). 'Low' = one mark per category (bars, cards, pies). Omit ONLY if the user has genuinely expressed no preference — omitting it is a proven no-op and the engine decides. This is a strong nudge, not a filter: it reorders charts that already fit, and an explicit chart_type still wins.

measures.description: Columns to treat as MEASURES (the PBI 'Values' well — fields the chart aggregates). Numeric non-identifier columns are measures by default.

non_additive.description: MEASURE columns that must NOT be summed (a ratio/average/rate — use mean, never stack). Usually auto-detected; this is an authoritative override.

out_dir.description: Optional directory to write chart.js/py, a data.sample.json, and (if preview_html) preview.html.

preview_html.description: Also emit a standalone D3 preview (needs out_dir). Default false — the code is meant to be merged, not run as an index.html.

privacy_level.description: How much detail to compute/share: 0 names only, 10 +counts, 20 +detailed stats (default), 30 +obfuscated sample rows.

project_dir.description: Directory to auto-detect the project language from (default: the folder setup_fabric_app used, else the working directory or the one project folder directly inside it).

prompt.description: Freeform guidance for the generation — the same 'user commentary' lane the Power BI visual uses. Steer encoding/axes/emphasis in plain language, e.g. 'put Year on the x-axis, color by Division', 'render citations as a chord diagram', 'log scale on revenue', 'annotate the peak'.

reasoning_mode.description: LLM pass structure; empty = backend heuristic.

renderer.description: Force a specific renderer (overrides `language`). Omit to use `language`/auto-detection; 'VISUAL'/'' = let the backend choose.

required_columns.description: Fields that MUST be visible in the output, each as its own column/channel. AUTHORITATIVE and VERIFIED: if the generated code never references one, the server regenerates automatically rather than returning a chart that silently dropped it.

rows_policy.description: 'auto' (default) = the engine decides how to summarize. 'all' = render EXACTLY one mark/row per source row, with no Top-N, no 'Other' rollup and no sampling. Use 'all' when your app depends on every row being present (a row-per-entity table, a point per location).

wrap.description: Code form: 'none' (default) = the raw render() function to merge; 'esm' = same code plus `export { render };` so the file can be `import`ed. Both forms are accepted everywhere - @bicharts/chart-host strips the export clause before compiling - so this is a convenience, never a compatibility choice.

name: generate_chart

binding.description: How `data` was built from your rows. Hand all three to @bicharts/chart-host - <BicChartGroup geo point destination> or createChartGroup(columns, rows, { geo, point, destination }) - and it builds the payload again from LIVE rows with the same columns; never rebuild __rowIdx__ or __geo* columns by hand.

destination.description: The same for a route's far end (an origin-destination flow map); point is then the origin. Null otherwise.

geo.description: The choropleth join: the column matched to the geometry and its kind. Null when nothing joins.

point.description: Which columns place a point (lat/lon, city, state, zip, country) and the map's gazetteer scope. Null when the chart places no points.

build.description: MCP server build stamp — the bundle actually serving this call.

chartName.description: The chart type the backend produced.

code.description: The render() source. Omitted when include_code is false.

codeSummary.description: The backend's own one-line description of what it built.

correlationId.description: Ties this generation to the server-side log — quote it in any support request.

creditCost.description: Credits billed, when the server reported them.

data.description: The render payload {columns, rows, …} to hand render() — INCLUDING any __geoIso__/__geoLat__/__geoLon__ columns the caller cannot reconstruct. Present only when out_dir was NOT given; otherwise read files.data.

dropLines.description: A 3D scatter's optional hover drop lines (a line from a hovered point to each back wall). requested: on, because the request asked; on/off: the user's answer, already applied to the generated component; ask: put askUser to the user ONCE before finishing, then pass hoverDropLines: true in the chart's options on a yes. Absent for every other chart.

files.description: Absolute paths written, when out_dir was given.

component.description: chart.component.tsx: the React host written with a D3 chart - the group, the binding, the plugins and the click contract wired, plus rowsFromTable for a query result. Render it instead of writing one.

column.description: Column joined to the geometry; null for a basemap-only point map.

hasGeometry.description: False means no bundled geometry matched this kind: the map will draw no land.

kind.description: Geometry asset kind — pass the matching geometry as options.geo.

unmatched.description: Regions in the data with no geometry match.

geo.description: Region/basemap wiring; null for non-geo charts.

ambiguousRows.description: Rows whose place name matched several places and was therefore NOT placed.

geoPoint.description: Point-geocoding outcome (a route's ORIGIN end when geoPointDest is present). `placed` counts only rows with a coordinate: neither an unplaced nor an ambiguous name is plotted. Null when the chart geocodes no points.

geoPointDest.description: A route's DESTINATION end (an origin-destination flow map), geocoded apart from geoPoint, which is then the origin. `placed` counts only rows with a destination coordinate: neither an unplaced nor an ambiguous name is plotted. Present only for a route.

ambiguousRows.description: Rows whose destination name matched several places and was therefore NOT placed.

hostContract.description: Host contract version the code targets; a host on a different MAJOR may not interoperate.

integrationContract.description: HOW TO RUN THIS CHART IN YOUR APP - the same integration contract the text block carries, here because a host that shows the model only this structured result would otherwise never see it: the payload and option shapes, the reference host (@bicharts/chart-host) with its React bindings AND its framework-free group (createChartGroup + createChartHost + attach) for a plain page or a UI framework reached through interop, this chart's d3 plugins and geometry, and the host-page prerequisites. Read it before wiring the chart in.

optionsRead.description: The option names THIS chart's code reads (sorted). A chart honours nothing it does not read, so a live restyle - host.setOptions({...}), never a regeneration - can only move these. Some are the host's to supply (width, height, geo, geoPoint, uiState, setUiState, themeFg/themeBg); the integration contract says what each one does. Empty for a non-D3 language.

outputHash.description: The server's identity for this exact code: the same code always carries the same hash. Keep it with the chart; it names the delivered code in a support request or a later report. Absent when the server sent none.

recoveredAfterMs.description: Present when the response stream was cut after the server accepted the request and this chart was then fetched back by its correlation: milliseconds from the start of the call to delivery. creditCost is null then, because the generation was charged as usual and the fetch that delivered it added the cached-serve fee.

requiredD3Plugins.description: D3 plugin PACKAGES this code calls (e.g. ["d3-sankey"]) — install them and pass the host ONE d3 that carries them, built with assembleD3(d3, { ...plugins }) from @bicharts/chart-host (assigning onto an ES-module d3 namespace throws), or the chart throws mid-render. Empty for core-only d3 and for non-D3 languages.

version.description: Server-side version number of this generation.

warningMessage.description: Present when the chart drawn is NOT the chart requested: names the requested type, the reason it was overruled, and what was drawn instead. Surface it to the user verbatim — never suppress it because the chart rendered fine.

title: Generate chart code
